universal_lens: Bayesian generative modeling of functional trajectories via infinite Dirichlet process Gaussian mixture models enables decomposition of play value into decision, execution, and coverage components through variational inference and conditional expectation.
gsi_mapping: GSI adopts the variational Bayesian framework to infer latent shot configurations from observed tracking data, enabling probabilistic attribution of decision quality (Shot IQ) and execution skill (VAST) via posterior predictive distributions over trajectory manifolds.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of Space-Time VON CRAMM lies in its use of a Bayesian generative model—specifically, an infinite Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixture Model—to represent the space of possible shot trajectories. This allows for probabilistic inference over latent shot configurations given observed tracking data. The key innovation is in decomposing play value into three orthogonal components: VAST (Value of All Shots Taken), which accounts for both decision and execution; Shot IQ, which isolates decision quality by marginalizing over execution; and VACC (Variance-Adjusted Court Coverage), which measures defensive contribution. These are derived through a three-stage process: first, generating plausible trajectories using the DP-GMM; second, conditioning these on observed states via closed-form multivariate normal updates; third, predicting outcomes using generalized additive models. The resulting ESV_t = ∫ P(W|A) P(A|X_t) dA enables continuous-time evaluation of shot value, supporting dynamic tactical reasoning. The mathematical structure mirrors that of a Bayesian belief network where trajectory arcs serve as latent variables, and outcome probabilities are computed via integration over these variables. Failure modes arise when trajectory smoothness assumptions break down or when outcome models misrepresent the relationship between shot features and results.
